$comment: The source of sf-include's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js), in the 1.4 form (scripts/generate-component-files.mjs writes rule.js, aliases.json, studio.fixture.json, studio.scenario.json, probe.json and smart.manifest.json from it). A new component, made against standard simai.smart-component 1.3.14 and vocabulary 1.1.5: step 3 of ui-control's control/LEGACY-UNITS-RETIREMENT-AND-NEW-PARTS-2026-11-02.md (owner decision q-410df7e4b5), the successor of the retired class units ajax, ajaxload and lazy-load.

src.summary: The address of the part: a page of the site's own server that answers with HTML. Same origin by default; another origin only when its server allows it by CORS. Changing it loads the new part; empty, nothing is fetched and the placeholder stays

load.summary: When the part is fetched: now, as soon as the element is on the page; view, once, when it comes within 200 px of the viewport (an IntersectionObserver; where there is none, at once)

lines.summary: How many text lines the placeholder skeleton draws while the part loads, when the page gives no placeholder of its own

loaded.summary: The part arrived and is on the page: src is the address as given, status the HTTP status. Sent after the markup is inserted, so a listener finds it in the element

load-failed.summary: The part did not arrive: reason network (the request failed, or another origin refused it by CORS; status null) or http (the server answered outside 200-299; status is its code). The element shows the error state with Retry

refresh.summary: Fetches src again now, whatever load says (vocabulary refresh: it re-reads). Answers applied when the part arrived, refused {reason: no-src | network | http} when there is no address or the load failed, cancelled when a newer load (a changed src, another refresh) replaced it or the element was removed. The Retry button of the error state calls it

placeholder.$comment:
Page content shown while the part loads, in place of the skeleton:
…
. A carrier whose only attribute is slot is unwrapped (the base's rule). It is the page's: placed as it is, never copied.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: The element is a plain region of the page: it has no role and no name of its own. It is aria-busy while the part loads (the skeleton is aria-hidden); the error message is a polite status, so it is announced, and Retry is a native button. The part's own markup brings its own roles.
accessibility.name: none

x-summary: Loads a part of the page from an address: a skeleton while it loads, the server's HTML in its place when it arrives (the Loader starts the components in it), an error with Retry when it does not. load="view" waits until the part nears the viewport.

x-source.brief: simai/ui-control control/LEGACY-UNITS-RETIREMENT-AND-NEW-PARTS-2026-11-02.md step 3 (owner decision q-410df7e4b5): replaces the class units ajax, ajaxload and lazy-load (audit control/evidence/2026-11-02-legacy-class-units.md: ajaxload polled every element once a second and filled it through BX.ajax.post, Bitrix only)

x-decisions: name: sf-include, not sf-fragment as the plan says. sf-fragment is a released, documented element already: core's interface-fragment boundary (src/core/js/composition/fragments.mjs defineFragmentBoundary, defined by core on every page; ui-doc guide/layouts/building/interface-fragments.md), and §21.4 refuses a second component with a taken name. include is the noun the web knows for a part of a page put in from another address (a server-side include).
family: content, a new one: the element holds a part of the page's content; none of the families shipped (state, skeleton, navigation) is it.

loading: fetch(src, {credentials: 'same-origin', headers: {Accept: 'text/html'}}), mode cors, so another origin answers only when its server allows it. One request at a time: a newer load aborts the older (AbortController on the instance's scope, §7.7), and a removed element aborts its request. No timer and no polling: load=view is one IntersectionObserver per element, rootMargin 200px, disconnected after its first sighting.

insertion: the answer is parsed in an inert <template> (a whole document: its body), its executable scripts are taken out (a <script> whose type is not JSON: a data-sf-settings island stays for the components inside), and so are inline event handlers (on* attributes) and javascript: addresses; the rest is drawn as the element's content with lit's unsafeHTML, as sf-modal draws its remote content. It is not a sanitizer: the part is the site's own markup. Untrusted HTML goes through SF.sanitizeHtml first.

components inside: the Loader's own MutationObserver scans the inserted markup like any markup added to the page (utilities, class components, Smart tags); the element also asks SF.Loader.ensureSmartElementLoaded for every Smart tag in the part that is not defined yet, so a part's components do not wait out the Loader's 100 ms debounce.
placeholder: an sf-skeleton of lines text lines (the last one 60 %), or the page's own slot placeholder in its place. While a part reloads (refresh, a new src) the placeholder shows again.

error: an icon, a short message in a polite status and an outline on-surface sf-button «Повторить» / «Retry» at the ladder's rung 1 that calls refresh. The words are the language files' own (runtime.failed, runtime.retry), not settings.

events: own verbs (vocabulary §5.1), loaded and load-failed, the fact forms copy-button's copied / copy-failed set. The action is refresh, the vocabulary's verb for reading again (§5), not reload: gate 11 refuses a synonym of a §5 verb.

first paint: the printed snapshot is what the element drew once its first load settled. A host printed with static markup keeps that picture until the first load settles (sfAwaitingData), then draws in one frame, so a printed part never flashes the skeleton between the server's picture and the element's.
host states: data-loading and data-failed (§5.3), besides aria-busy on the region while it loads.

css-variables: six public variables (§6) -- the placeholder's minimum block size, and the error state's gap, padding, border colour, radius and message colour -- listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json; the Framework never sets one.

version 1.0.2 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.0.3 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint snapshots follow the actions block (docs review R031, R032; decisions C13-C15): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws ask for the screen-reader-only utility sheet (sf-button 1.9.0, sf-button-icon 1.7.0), an sf-button-close it draws asks for its own sheet (C14), and sf-input's classes follow its outer sizes (sf-input 1.6.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

forbidden_client_responsibilities: deciding who may see the part (the server answers it, or refuses with a status)

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-include to put a part of the page that the site's server answers at an address into the page: a news block, a list rendered on the server, a part below the fold loaded once it nears the viewport (load="view").
do_not: Do not use sf-include for data a component asks a host for; a host port does that
Do not rely on scripts in the answer: they are not run; put the behaviour into components, which the Loader starts
Do not load untrusted HTML into it; clean it with SF.sanitizeHtml and draw it yourself
Do not poll an address with it; refresh() reloads when the page asks

keyboard: Tab reaches Retry in the error state
accessibility.focus: Focus on Retry moves to the region (tabindex -1) while the part loads again, so it never falls to the page; a new failure hands it to the new Retry.
